title: How to Build Secure AI Agents with Least Privilege, Sandboxing, Policy Enforcement, and Prompt Injection Defense
existing_summary: This deep dive explores how to prevent prompt injection, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, and uncontrolled infrastructure access while preserving useful agent autonomy.
summary_bullets: Treat AI agents as untrusted code running inside a security appliance rather than trusted executables
Separate reasoning from execution—give agents narrowly scoped, predefined operations rather than shell access or raw credentials
Implement deny-by-default outbound networking and use workload identities with time-limited privileges to contain potential breaches
Apply sandboxing layers (containers, gVisor, microVMs) proportional to workload hostility and implement strict memory provenance controls
Place policy enforcement outside the model layer through IAM, policy engines, and approval gates rather than relying on prompts or instructions
